# Weekly Updates

Each club sends one written update per week. It goes to Soraya Cullimore and is published on
the Strategy Program website, so it serves two audiences at once: the person who supervises
the co-president pairs, and the students across campus who want to know what the clubs are
doing.

This is graded. It is the only deliverable in the course that produces a public artifact.

## Who Sends It

One update per club per week, sent by one of the two co-presidents. The pair alternates
weeks, so each co-president writes six updates across the semester. WSA has a single
president, who sends every week.

| Club | Sent by |
|---|---|
| MCA | Co-presidents, alternating weeks |
| PMA | Co-presidents, alternating weeks |
| CSA | Co-presidents, alternating weeks |
| WSA | President, weekly |

Decide your rotation in week one and keep it. A missed week counts against the club, not
against whichever co-president happened to be up.

## Deadline

**Thursday by 11:59 PM**

Thursday rather than the weekend, so the updates are in hand before Friday's session. What
you write becomes the Announcements block: if your club has an event, a deadline, or a
problem the room should know about, the update is how it gets there.

- First update due: Thu, Sep 10, ahead of session 2
- Final update due: Thu, Dec 3, ahead of session 13
- No update due Thu, Nov 26. Thanksgiving, and there is no class Nov 27.
- Total updates per club: 12

Session 1 on Sep 4 is the kickoff, so there is no update before it. Every session after that
has one.

## Recipients

- **To:** Soraya Cullimore
- **CC:** Scott Murff, your faculty advisor, your co-president
- **Also:** submitted for publication on the Strategy Program website

Write it knowing it will be public. Nothing goes in a weekly update that you would not want a
prospective member, a recruiter, or a firm contact to read.

## Format

Four sections. The first three mirror the APM Lab weekly update; the fourth exists because
these clubs serve students, not a single manager.

**1. What we did this week [Required]**

- Completed events, meetings, outreach, and deliverables
- Lead with outcomes, not activity. "42 students at the case workshop" beats "held a case
  workshop."
- Include numbers when you have them: attendance, applications, offers, signups

**2. What we are doing next week [Required]**

- Priorities and planned events, with owners
- Be realistic about what fits in a week

**3. Blockers, risks, or dependencies [Omit if none]**

- Anything that might slow you down
- What you need from Soraya, your advisor, or another club
- Decisions you are waiting on

**4. What students should know [Required]**

- The part that gets published. Upcoming events with dates, deadlines, and how to
  participate.
- Written for a student who is not in your club and may not be a strategy major. Spell out
  acronyms and say what the event is for.

## Example

```
Subject: PMA Weekly Update - Week of Sep 8

Hi Soraya,

What we did this week:
- Ran the PM resume workshop, 38 students attended, 22 from outside the strategy major
- Confirmed Adobe for the Oct 2 info session
- Sent 14 alumni outreach emails, 6 replies so far

Next week:
- Finalize the fall mentorship pairings (Maya owns this)
- Post the case competition signup form
- First mock interview round, Thursday evening

Blockers:
- Still need a room for Oct 2, the request has been pending two weeks
- Our marketing VP is out for a family emergency through the 20th

What students should know:
- PMA is hosting an Adobe info session Thu, Oct 2 at 5:00 PM in the Tanner Building.
  Open to any major. No signup required.
- Mentorship applications close Fri, Sep 19. Anyone interested in product management
  can apply, first or fourth year, any major.

Thanks,
[Name]
```

## Grading

Twelve updates. Points and category weight are set on the
[Assessments](00-assessments.qmd) page.

| Status | Credit |
|---|---|
| On time, Thursday by 11:59 PM | Full |
| Late, by Friday 12:30 PM (start of class) | Half |
| After class starts | None |

The late cutoff is the start of class because an update that arrives after the session has
already missed its second job, which is feeding the room.

## What Makes a Good Update

- **Short.** Bullets, not paragraphs. If it runs past one screen, cut it.
- **Specific.** Numbers, names, dates. "Good turnout" tells Soraya nothing.
- **Honest about blockers.** Flagging a problem early is the entire point. A clean update
  every week from a club that is struggling is worse than no update.
- **Consistent.** The value is in the streak. Twelve on-time updates build a record of the
  semester that nobody has to reconstruct in December.
